answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake that is slashed on proven fraud, like a jade deposit held in escrow: creating thousands of fake agents then costs real capital per identity, and a saffron-flagged reputation score decays unless the agent keeps doing useful, verified work. Newcomers start on a low-trust terrace with capped transaction value, earning higher limits only through attested history, so an attacker must pay the stake and the time cost for every fake identity instead of spawning them free.
